correctness.rationale: For any dominating D, the complement of the B-pair projection of its one-A layer has every triangle selected in the all-B layer; removing one edge per triangle and applying the proved Mantel bound gives q(n). A four-family witness of size q(n)+(binom(m-1,2)+1)n-2 dominates all 0,1,2,3-A configurations, including m=2 and n=4. Fixed-m squeeze proves asymptotic 1/4. The self-contained checker directly verifies 95 constructions, triangle-deletion counts for 33,864 graphs, and exhaustive K_2,4 lower boundary. Finite tests are not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The primary published 2026 manuscript treats the exact same three-token bipartite graph but supplies only bounds with the wrong leading constants/order at fixed m; the new sharp 1/4 coefficient comes from a full one-A-token-pair Mantel obstruction plus a matching leading-term four-layer construction. Complete-graph three-token results and two-token bipartite exact results cannot imply the claim. A specifically referenced unpublished work in progress on this question remains a material priority risk: no historical uniqueness is certified.
residual_risks: The arXiv:2610.31557 concluding bibliography points to L. M. Rivera, "Domination in k-token graphs of complete bipartite graphs and Turán numbers", described as work in progress. No public full text or theorem statement was verified. It could independently contain overlapping or stronger results, so historical priority is not settled.
No semantic-index search can exclude all equivalent unpublished or unindexed results; only checked public literature and accessible records are compared.
The older token-graph independence/matching paper was screened only via its abstract and cannot support a full-document noncoverage claim.

value.rationale: An explicit fresh 2026 paper leaves three-token complete-bipartite domination between broad generic bounds that fail to determine even the leading upper-order coefficient at fixed m. An exact quadratic asymptotic with sharp leading constant 1/4 and an O_m(n) gap for every fixed m is a natural substantial infinite family result. The core triangle-free projection and simultaneous four-layer witness convey structural understanding; no exact finite optimum or independent historical priority is claimed.
